title: OpenManaProtocol
description: The only contract between the OpenMana UI and the engine (Forge bridge in a Dedicated Worker). Three directions: EngineMessage (worker -> page, postMessage), EngineInput (page -> engine, SharedArrayBuffer input queue) and WorkerCommand (page -> worker, postMessage while the worker is idle). The UI sees no Forge classes; Forge alone decides rules, legal actions and AI. Any change to this file is a new protocol version: bump ProtocolVersion and Protocol.VERSION in the bridge together, then run `npm run generate` in engine/.

ProtocolVersion.title: ProtocolVersion
ProtocolVersion.description: Version of this contract. UI, worker host and engine must speak exactly the same version; anything else is refused loudly (engine.abort, reason protocol-mismatch). 2: engine language (boot argument --language, BootReport.language), EngineBuild.resourcesSha256, diagnostics.card-probe. 3: engine trace for the differential tests (MatchRequest.trace, DiagnosticsAiMatchCommand.trace, diagnostics.trace, MatchSummary.trace, AiMatchResult.trace). 4: card language (boot argument --card-language, BootReport.cardLanguage) and Forge's AI profiles (BootReport.aiProfiles; match.start with any other profile is refused). 5: priority, stack and phases (prompt 16): a stack item carries its card as Forge shows it (StackItem.card) and says whether it is an ability (StackItem.ability), its source id only for a card the player may see; Forge's buttons of the priority step say what they do (Button.meaning); a selection's cards are only those the player may see.

EngineMessage.title: EngineMessage
EngineMessage.description: Everything the worker posts to the page: lifecycle messages of the worker host (engine.*, match.finished, diagnostics.*) and the game messages of the bridge.

EngineInput.title: EngineInput
EngineInput.description: What the player does, written into the SharedArrayBuffer input queue. Forge reads one input whenever it waits for the player. `seq` numbers the inputs of a match from 1 without gaps; the bridge refuses to continue if the sequence breaks (technical abort).

WorkerCommand.title: WorkerCommand
WorkerCommand.description: Commands the page posts to the worker. The worker handles them only while it is idle (before and between Forge calls); during a match everything goes through the input queue.

EngineBoot.title: EngineBoot
EngineBoot.description: Progress while the engine starts (for a loading indicator and start-up timings).

BootPhase.title: BootPhase
BootPhase.description: worker-features: the worker checked the browser; launcher-load: the engine launcher script is loading; wasm-fetch-compile: the ~70 MB module is fetched and compiled; java-main: Forge unpacks its data and initialises.

WorkerTime.title: WorkerTime
WorkerTime.description: Milliseconds since the worker started (worker clock).

FeatureReport.title: FeatureReport
FeatureReport.description: What the runtime supports. The engine needs WebAssembly GC, exception handling with exnref and typed function references (GraalVM Web Image), a Dedicated Worker, SharedArrayBuffer with Atomics.wait and, in browsers, cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP).

crossOriginIsolated.description: null where the runtime has no such notion (Node).

missing.description: Human-readable names of the missing features (German).

EngineReady.title: EngineReady
EngineReady.description: Forge is initialised and waits for match.start. Carries the protocol version (checked before anything else) and which engine build this is.

EngineBuild.title: EngineBuild
EngineBuild.description: Build facts of the engine: pinned Forge, patch queue, OpenMana commit.

engineSourcesModified.description: true if engine/ had uncommitted changes when the engine was built.

synchronous.description: Forge runs in synchronous mode (patch 0001); must be true.

resourcesSha256.description: SHA-256 of the Forge data bundle compiled into this engine (engine-manifest.json, resources.sha256).

BootReport.title: BootReport
BootReport.description: How the engine started: Forge's data unpacked, Forge initialised, card loading, the language Forge speaks (language) and the language of the cards in its texts and card views (cardLanguage: names, type lines, rules texts; boot argument --card-language, by default the language), the AI profiles Forge loaded.

aiProfiles.description: The AI profiles Forge loaded (res/ai/*.ai), each once, sorted by name. MatchRequest.ai.profile must be one of them.

CardLoading.title: CardLoading
CardLoading.description: How Forge reads its card scripts (boot argument --card-loading; default eager). eager: every card is read and indexed at start; lazy: only a name index at start, a card's script when it is first needed, and the whole database the first time an effect or decision needs all cards (a random card, the player naming a card), which stalls the game for tens of seconds in the browser.

EngineLanguage.title: EngineLanguage
EngineLanguage.description: A language of Forge: the language it speaks (boot argument --language: its own messages - prompts, buttons, game log) or the language of the cards in them and in its card views (boot argument --card-language: names, type lines, rules texts; by default the same). Card keys (Card.key) stay English in every language.

EngineWaiting.title: EngineWaiting
EngineWaiting.description: The engine found the input queue empty and now waits for the player. `consumed` inputs have been read so far; every input up to that number is completely processed (a rejection, if any, was posted before this message). While the engine waits it is not stalled.

EngineError.title: EngineError
EngineError.description: A command failed, the engine stays usable. After deck-rejected or invalid-request the same worker accepts a new match.start.

EngineErrorCode.title: EngineErrorCode
EngineErrorCode.description: deck-rejected: Forge cannot build a deck (report names every card it does not know or support; nothing is dropped silently); invalid-request: the match request does not fit the contract; not-ready: match.start before engine.ready; already-started: this worker already ran a game (one game per worker, Forge's state is static).

EngineAbort.title: EngineAbort
EngineAbort.description: Technical abort: the engine cannot continue and the worker is terminated. This is not a game result; a running game ends without one. origin tells whether the worker reported it or the client detected it (worker error, watchdog, contract violation, abort by the UI).

MatchFinished.title: MatchFinished
MatchFinished.description: Forge returned from the match (after game.end). Technical summary for diagnostics and tests; the UI shows game.end.

MatchSummary.title: MatchSummary
MatchSummary.description: logSha256: hash of Forge's complete game log (equal on JVM and Wasm for the same seed and inputs); protocolSha256: fingerprint of every decision message (all but state and events); forgeCallbacks: Forge's calls into the GUI by method; trace: only for a traced match (MatchRequest.trace), how many trace entries and events the engine sent.

inputs.description: Inputs Forge read during the match.

forgeCallbacks.description: Forge's calls into the GUI, counted by method.

DiagnosticsTrace.title: DiagnosticsTrace
DiagnosticsTrace.description: Engine tests only (differential tests, prompt 05): one entry of the engine trace, sent during a match whose request asked for it (MatchRequest.trace) or during a traced diagnostics.ai-match. A structured, language-independent record of the game for comparing the JVM and the WebAssembly engine: a checkpoint with a complete snapshot plus every event since the previous entry. It contains hidden information (libraries, the AI's hand) and is never shown to a player.

inputs.description: Inputs the engine had read at this checkpoint.

TraceCheckpoint.title: TraceCheckpoint
TraceCheckpoint.description: Where an entry was taken: input = Forge waits for the player's next input; phase = a step of a turn begins; end = Forge finished the game. None depends on a clock.

TraceEventKind.title: TraceEventKind
TraceEventKind.description: Forge's game events (bridge TraceEvents: one kind per Forge event class, e.g. cast, resolve, move, attackers, blockers, damage, mana, priority, phase, log) and the bridge's own: started (game.started), question, withdrawn, answered, rejected (input.rejected), message (kind only), end (game.end), input (what the engine read).

TraceEvent.title: TraceEvent
TraceEvent.description: One event of the engine trace. e is its kind; the other fields are ids, English card keys (key: Forge's oracle name), references (c<card id>, p<player id>, <ZoneType>:<player id>), enum names and numbers - never Forge's display texts. A diagnostics record, compared as a whole; its fields depend on the kind.

TraceSnapshot.title: TraceSnapshot
TraceSnapshot.description: The complete game at a checkpoint, from Forge's model: every zone of every player (the library in order and hidden hands included), the stack with targets, combat. In a human game also human (the human seat), gui (Forge's markers for that seat) and questions (the open ones, without words).

mana.description: Mana in the pool; only colours with an amount.

damage.description: Player id -> combat damage this commander dealt to that player.

TraceCard.title: TraceCard
TraceCard.description: A card outside the battlefield: id, English key (Forge's oracle name), the face it shows if not its original one.

TraceStackItem.title: TraceStackItem
TraceStackItem.description: api: what the effect does (Forge's ApiType, e.g. DealDamage), not its text.

TraceMarkers.title: TraceMarkers
TraceMarkers.description: What Forge marked for the human seat's GUI (look-ups in the GUI's own sets): playable (weakly selectable), highlighted, selectable.

TraceQuestion.title: TraceQuestion
TraceQuestion.description: A question without its words (text, button labels, card views): kind, limits, flags and what its items refer to.

suggested.description: Forge's suggestion unless it is text: a boolean (confirm), a number (options) or item numbers (choose, order).

TraceItemRef.title: TraceItemRef
TraceItemRef.description: What an item stands for: c<card id>, p<player id>, hidden (a card the player may not see) or #<item number> (only words).

TraceTarget.title: TraceTarget
TraceTarget.description: c<card id>, p<player id> or s<card id> (a spell on the stack, by its card; s? if it has none).

TraceSummary.title: TraceSummary
TraceSummary.description: How many trace entries and events the engine sent (the receiver must have them all).

CardProbeResult.title: CardProbeResult
CardProbeResult.description: Forge's card scripts checked inside the engine (bridge CardProbe): effects that create cards by name, representative cards of every layout, every token script, the newest editions and every card of the database turned into game cards. fingerprint covers everything except language and millis and must be equal on the JVM and in the browser for the same engine and card loading mode; sections holds the same per section. failures lists everything that must fail a test. The objects inside the sections are free-form diagnostics (not a UI contract).

scriptWarnings.description: What Forge printed about broken card scripts while building the game cards (upstream data problems, equal on every runtime).

CardProbeDatabasePass.title: CardProbeDatabasePass
CardProbeDatabasePass.description: One card database (regular or variant cards) turned completely into game cards.

cardNames.description: The card names of BOTH decks in one sorted list without owner (image prefetch without revealing the AI's deck).

GameState.title: GameState
GameState.description: The complete game as the player may see it: always a full snapshot, never a delta. The UI replaces its previous state with it.

Phase.title: Phase
Phase.description: Step of the turn (Magic's turn structure). null before the first turn (mulligan).

canAct.description: Forge: the player has anything to do at all right now.

library.description: Only the size; the library never leaves the engine.

Card.title: Card
Card.description: A card the player may see (VisibleCard) or only knows exists (HiddenCard). Forge decides visibility (mayView).

HiddenCard.title: HiddenCard
HiddenCard.description: Only that there is a card: no id (ids follow the deck list and would reveal the card), no name.

VisibleCard.title: VisibleCard
VisibleCard.description: A card as Forge shows it to the player. key is the English oracle name (stable identity for Scryfall); name, typeLine and text are Forge's display texts. colors/printedColors only if the current colours differ from the printed ones. playable, action, ways and highlighted are Forge's own markers; the UI never computes them.

text.description: Rules text; only on the battlefield, in the command zone, in the player's own hand and in card views of questions.

printedColors.description: Printed colours (empty = colourless), only together with colors.

playable.description: Forge: something can be done with this card now.

action.description: Forge: what tapping the card would do now, in Forge's words.

ways.description: Forge: all ways to use this playable card (e.g. cast or an alternative cost).

highlighted.description: Forge's highlight (e.g. cards chosen for the bottom during the London mulligan).

ColorLetters.title: ColorLetters
ColorLetters.description: Colours as WUBRG letters in this order, at least one.

StackItem.title: StackItem
StackItem.description: A spell or ability on the stack (the state's stack is top first: the first item resolves next). text is Forge's own description of it.

source.description: The id of the spell's card or of the ability's source; null if Forge names none or the player may not see it.

card.description: That card as Forge shows it to the player: a spell's own card (it lies on the stack, which is no zone of the state), an ability's source; hidden if the player may not see it (a face-down spell); null if Forge names no card. Never marked as usable: a card on the stack is not tapped.

ability.description: Forge: an activated or triggered ability (trigger says which), not a spell.

CombatEntry.title: CombatEntry
CombatEntry.description: An attacker, whom it attacks and its blockers (while blockers are declared: Forge's planned blockers). Player and card ids are separate ranges, hence defenderKind.

GameEvents.title: GameEvents
GameEvents.description: New entries of Forge's game log (verbosity MEDIUM), sent BEFORE the state they explain.

GameEvent.title: GameEvent
GameEvent.description: One log entry. card: the source card, only if the player may see it.

kind.description: Forge's log entry type (e.g. LAND, STACK_ADD, DAMAGE).

actor.description: Who did it, from structured data; absent if unknown.

GameMessage.title: GameMessage
GameMessage.description: Text Forge shows the player. prompt: the instruction line of the current decision; notice: a message dialog; error: an error dialog; incorrect-action: Forge refused an action (flash, empty text). cardView: the full card, because while a spell is being paid for it is in no zone.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: A decision Forge asks for. Every question is closed by exactly one question.withdrawn or question.answered. blocking: while it is open, only it can be answered (taps and other answers are rejected as not-active); state.request and concede still work.

QuestionId.title: QuestionId
QuestionId.description: Strictly increasing within a match, never reused.

SelectQuestion.title: SelectQuestion
SelectQuestion.description: Forge names cards that may be selected now (targets, cards to discard ...). Answering taps the chosen items like clicks; the question stays open until Forge changes or clears the selection. No card = the target is a player (player.tap).

cards.description: The ids of the selectable cards the player may see; a hidden one is only a hidden item (ids follow the deck lists).

ButtonsQuestion.title: ButtonsQuestion
ButtonsQuestion.description: Forge's two prompt buttons (OK/Cancel, Keep/Mulligan ...). purpose says what they are for, from Forge's own labels and running input.

ButtonMeaning.title: ButtonMeaning
ButtonMeaning.description: What one of Forge's buttons does, where the bridge knows it from Forge's own label keys (the priority step): pass = pass priority (Forge's OK), endTurn = pass priority until the end of this turn (Forge's End Turn), undo = take back the last action (Forge's Undo). Absent elsewhere.

OptionsQuestion.title: OptionsQuestion
OptionsQuestion.description: One option out of a list. With revealed it is a list to look at with a single OK. option 0 cancels, only if cancellable.

OrderQuestion.title: OrderQuestion
OrderQuestion.description: Forge's dual list: the answer lists the chosen items in order, the rest remains. How many must remain: remainingMin..remainingMax (negative maximum = any number; both 0 = order all).

ArrangeQuestion.title: ArrangeQuestion
ArrangeQuestion.description: Move cards of a hidden pile to its top or bottom (scry and similar). Only the movable cards are sent; others is the number of the rest.

toAnywhere.description: Forge would allow any position; not offered yet (prompt 15).

Item.title: Item
Item.description: One entry of a question's list, numbered from 1. A card the player may not see is only {nr, hidden: true}.

QuestionWithdrawn.title: QuestionWithdrawn
QuestionWithdrawn.description: Forge no longer asks this question (it changed the buttons or selection, the input ended, the game is over). Normal, not an error; an answer to it is rejected as stale.

QuestionAnswered.title: QuestionAnswered
QuestionAnswered.description: The answer with this seq was accepted and closed the question. (Answers to a select question never close it; Forge withdraws it when the selection is complete.)

InputRejected.title: InputRejected
InputRejected.description: An input was NOT carried out. Nothing disappears silently: the UI must show it.

RejectReason.title: RejectReason
RejectReason.description: stale: the question is not open (withdrawn, answered or unknown); not-active: a blocking question must be answered first; invalid: the answer does not fit its question (kind, range, count, sum, disabled button); malformed: unknown input type; unknown-card: no card with this id is visible to the player; unknown-player: no such player; no-effect: Forge did not accept the tap in the current step.

GameEnd.title: GameEnd
GameEnd.description: The game is over. result is from the player's point of view. All questions are closed before this message.

Seq.title: Seq
Seq.description: Number of an input within the match, from 1, without gaps.

AnswerInput.title: AnswerInput
AnswerInput.description: Answer to an open question. kind must be the question's kind.

SelectAnswer.title: SelectAnswer
SelectAnswer.description: Item numbers to tap, 1..max of them.

ChooseAnswer.title: ChooseAnswer
ChooseAnswer.description: Distinct item numbers, min..max of them.

OptionsAnswer.title: OptionsAnswer
OptionsAnswer.description: Item number, or 0 to cancel a cancellable question.

InputAnswer.title: InputAnswer
InputAnswer.description: Text; a whole number if the question is numeric.

OrderAnswer.title: OrderAnswer
OrderAnswer.description: Chosen item numbers in order; the rest remains (see OrderQuestion).

ArrangeAnswer.title: ArrangeAnswer
ArrangeAnswer.description: Every item exactly once, either to the top or to the bottom, each list in order.

DistributeAnswer.title: DistributeAnswer
DistributeAnswer.description: One amount per item (parallel to items), each at least min, summing to total.

CardTapInput.title: CardTapInput
CardTapInput.description: Tap a card without being asked: this is how cards are played at priority, paid with, declared as attackers or blockers. Forge decides what the tap means.

PlayerTapInput.title: PlayerTapInput
PlayerTapInput.description: Tap a player (e.g. a player as target).

StateRequestInput.title: StateRequestInput
StateRequestInput.description: Ask for a fresh full state; served at once, even while a blocking question waits.

ConcedeInput.title: ConcedeInput
ConcedeInput.description: Concede the game. Is the decision itself: no second confirmation from the engine (the UI confirms before sending).

EngineStartCommand.title: EngineStartCommand
EngineStartCommand.description: Start the engine in this (fresh) worker. The worker checks the protocol version first, then the runtime features, then the input queue, and only then loads the ~70 MB engine.

args.description: Boot arguments of the engine: --card-loading=eager|lazy (default eager), --language=en-US|de-DE (default en-US), --card-language=en-US|de-DE (default: the language). Anything else stops the boot (engine.abort boot-failed).

queue.description: The SharedArrayBuffer of the input queue (see input-queue.ts for its layout).

requireIsolation.description: Require crossOriginIsolated (browsers: yes; Node tests: no).

DiagnosticsAiMatchCommand.title: DiagnosticsAiMatchCommand
DiagnosticsAiMatchCommand.description: Engine tests only: Forge's AI plays itself with fixed smoke decks. trace: the engine also sends its trace (diagnostics.trace) during the game.

DiagnosticsCardProbeCommand.title: DiagnosticsCardProbeCommand
DiagnosticsCardProbeCommand.description: Engine tests only: check that Forge's card scripts load and become game cards (answered with diagnostics.cards).

MatchRequest.title: MatchRequest
MatchRequest.description: A game human (through this protocol) against Forge's AI. Decks come from the UI (IndexedDB later), card names in English (front face of double-faced cards). ai.profile: one of the engine's AI profiles (BootReport.aiProfiles, Forge's res/ai/*.ai), e.g. Default; any other is refused (engine.error invalid-request) instead of Forge silently playing its built-in defaults.

seed.description: Fixed seed for reproducible games (tests); absent or null = random.

trace.description: Engine tests only (differential tests, prompt 05): the engine also sends its trace (diagnostics.trace), which contains hidden information. The UI never sets it.

CardId.title: CardId
CardId.description: Forge's card id (unique within a game).
